subject: FinPay: Competitive TCO follow-up & proposed POC
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: FinPay: Competitive TCO follow-up & proposed POC

Hi Emma — great to meet you and the team today. Quick recap from our discovery + suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost and latency for FinPay's real-time assist flows while keeping answer quality high and predictable.
- Key constraints: PCI-sensitive data in prompts, 95th perc latency target < 300ms, and procurement timeline in March.

High-level Redwood differentiators we discussed:
- Unified runtime across Hosted / Dedicated / Private (helps with compliance and rollouts)
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, prefix/KV cache that avoids re-generation, and quantization profiles tuned for production workloads
- Smart routing + fallbacks to lower-cost variants to preserve availability

Proposed immediate next steps (POC scope):
1) Cost/latency baseline run vs hyperscaler (open model + shared comparator): generate per-1M token unit economics with matched model quality and 95th/avg latency.
2) Cache-hit experiments: measure prefix cache hit rates on a 2-week sample; run with and without cache to show delta.
3) Batching/throughput tests: run max throughput and 95th p99 latency sweeps to show production SLOs.

I've attached a brief pricing workbook and a draft mutual action plan. Can we kick off the POC next Monday (2/22)? If that works, I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff and loop in our infra/solutions team.

Notes on high-level unit economics (see attached spreadsheet for full calc):
- Assumptions: average request ~1k tokens (payload + response), 1M tokens = ~1,000 requests.
- Quick comparator (generation token costs): Redwood Hosted baseline: ~$25 / 1M tokens. With caching (30% prefix hits) effective cost ~ $17.5 / 1M.
- Hyperscaler (public API typical list): OpenAI-like: ~$42 / 1M; AWS Bedrock-like: ~$38 / 1M.
- Dedicated/Reserved (Redwood Dedicated): at commit sizes typical for FinPay, amortized cost can drop to ~$6-8 / 1M tokens (includes infra amortization + ops).

I can refine these numbers against your telemetry if you share a 1-week sample or estimated QPS/avg tokens.

Next actions: please confirm POC kickoff date and whether procurement needs a formal SOW/quote ahead of kickoff.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, procurement@finpay.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinPay: Competitive TCO follow-up & proposed POC

Emma — good questions. Detailed assumptions below (I'll also attach the spreadsheet tab with the line-by-line calc):

Common assumptions we will use for the POC (and how they affect per-1M token numbers):
- Unit: 1M generated tokens (generation = model output tokens; prompts billed separately in some vendors — our workbook normalizes to total token count).
- Avg tokens per request: 1,000 total tokens (payload + response). If your workload is smaller/larger we'll recompute.
- Cache model: prefix/KV cache that avoids re-generation for repeated system prompts and deterministic prefixes. We categorize prefixes into: system prompts (high reuse), canned responses (medium), user-specific history (low).
- Batching: continuous batching improves GPU utilization; effective throughput increases with request concurrency. For cost per 1M tokens we assume realistic batching at production (avg effective batch size ~8).

Redwood numbers (hosted API):
- Baseline generation cost (no cache): $25 / 1M tokens (this is our hosted, model-optimized path using quantized kernels and batching).
- With cache: at 30% prefix hit rate -> effective generation tokens = 700k -> effective cost = $17.5 / 1M tokens.
- With higher cache (60% hit) -> effective cost = $10 / 1M tokens.

Hyperscaler comparators (public list-rate style):
- OpenAI-like: ~$42 / 1M (no local cache savings unless you add an additional caching layer).
- AWS Bedrock-like: ~$38 / 1M.

Dedicated/Reserved (Redwood Dedicated model):
- At commit sizes typical for enterprise POCs (6-12 month reserved GPU pools), the amortized token cost can fall in the $6-8 / 1M range depending on utilization and model choice. This assumes you control keys, private networking and we commit to a baseline throughput.

Other factors that change unit economics:
- Latency SLOs: lower-latency targets can reduce batching headroom and increase cost/prediction. We'll measure 95th at target SLO to show the true cost at your latency requirements.
- Batchability: workloads with lots of short single-request sessions (low batching) will naturally cost more per token than highly batchable workloads.
- Cache hit mix: if a large portion of traffic are repeated prompts (system messages), cache has outsized impact.

Proposed test matrix for POC (we will instrument and produce a final TCO report):
A) Baseline: run identical prompt set against Redwood hosted and Hyperscaler endpoint at matched concurrency; measure cost / 1M, 95th latency, and quality metrics (same eval prompts).
B) Cache sensitivity: run with cache off / on; measure hit rate and delta cost/latency.
C) Batch sweep: vary concurrency to show cost vs latency trade-offs and estimate effective amortized cost at your anticipated QPS.
D) Dedicated cost model: produce a modeled cost spreadsheet that shows break-even point between hosted vs dedicated at your monthly token volume.

I'll bring Marcus (solutions) and Marissa (pricing) to the kickoff to validate the plan and SOW. Attached is the workbook with the line items; I can also export a procurement-ready two-page SOW if procurement wants that before kickoff.

If that all sounds right, I'll schedule the 2/22 kickoff (30 min) and include the PoC checklist.

Best,
Aditya

Looping in a quick internal checklist so we can be ready for the Monday kickoff: 
- Marissa: please validate the dedicated amortization model and prepare a 6/12 month cost sheet (we need a banded table: 50% util, 75% util, 90% util -> $/1M tokens).
- Infra: prepare a hosted test endpoint with the model variants we'll show (quantized 70B, float 13B) and enable prefix cache instrumentation + logging.
- Solutions: confirm test harness (we'll need 2M test tokens for the baseline runs and 5M for batch sweeps).
- Legal/Procurement: request a short SOW template for POC (1 page) and the standard IP/NDAs if needed.

Also note: include a column in the spreadsheet that shows cost sensitivity to batch size (batch size 1,4,8,16). That will help FinPay see the latency/cost trade-offs.

-Marcus
